description: Company Description South Agricultural Research Institute is a public research organization dedicated to advancing sustainable agricultural development in the southern regions of the country. The Institute focuses on improving crop productivity, livestock management, natural resource conservation, and climate-resilient farming systems. It works closely with local communities, government agencies, and development partners to generate practical, evidence-based solutions for farmers. Staff members have opportunities to contribute to impactful research, capacity building, and technology transfer that directly support rural livelihoods and food security. This full-time, hybrid role is based in Jinka, with a combination of on-site work at research stations and limited work-from-home flexibility for tasks such as data analysis, report writing, and virtual collaboration. Day-to-day responsibilities include developing research proposals, securing ethical and institutional approvals, supervising field experiments and surveys, managing research teams, and ensuring data quality. The Senior Researcher will prepare technical reports, policy briefs, and peer-reviewed publications, present results to stakeholders, and support the translation of research outcomes into practical recommendations for farmers and extension services. The role also involves mentoring junior researchers, building partnerships with academic and development organizations, and contributing to strategic planning within the Institute. Qualifications Advanced degree (preferably PhD or MSc) in agriculture, agronomy, plant sciences, animal sciences, natural resource management, or a related field. Demonstrated experience in designing and leading field-based agricultural research projects, including experimental design, data collection, and analysis. Strong skills in scientific writing, report preparation, and publication in peer-reviewed journals. Proficiency in data analysis tools and statistical software (e.g., R, SPSS, STATA, or similar), and ability to interpret and communicate results clearly. Experience supervising multidisciplinary teams, mentoring junior staff, and coordinating with field technicians and extension personnel. Proven ability to engage with farmers, local communities, and stakeholders, and to translate research findings into practical recommendations. Solid understanding of sustainable agriculture, climate-resilient practices, and rural development challenges in similar contexts. Excellent organizational skills, ability to manage multiple projects and deadlines, and work effectively in a hybrid setting (on-site in Jinka and remote as needed). Strong written and verbal communication skills in English; knowledge of local languages is an advantage. Willingness to travel within the region for fieldwork and stakeholder engagement activities.

title: Consultancy for the adaptation and finalization of the EMAP+ resource package for Ethiopia (POWER program)
description: The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world's worst humanitarian crises, helping to restore health, safety, education, economic wellbeing, and power to people devastated by conflict and disaster. Founded in 1933 at the call of Albert Einstein, the IRC is one of the world's largest international humanitarian non-governmental organizations (INGO), at work in more than 40 countries and 29 U.S. cities helping people to survive, reclaim control of their future and strengthen their communities. A force for humanity, IRC employees deliver lasting impact by restoring safety, dignity and hope to millions. If you're a solutions-driven, passionate change-maker, come join us in positively impacting the lives of millions of people world-wide for a better future. Consultancy — Terms of Reference (ToR) Adaptation and finalization of the EMAP+ resource package for Ethiopia Assignment title: Consultancy for the adaptation and finalization of the EMAP+ resource package for Ethiopia (POWER program) Total number of consultants: One (1) Focus country: Ethiopia, within the multi-country POWER program Program: POWER program (2025–2027), supported by Irish Aid Anchoring / reporting: Global Violence Prevention and Response Unit (VPRU) / East Africa VPR regional Lead in coordination with IRC WPE Coordinator and EA WPE Technical Advisor Proposed dates: [to be confirmed] Duration: Approximately 6 weeks (level of effort to be confirmed) Location: Remote (home-based) Background of the project The Women's Protection and Empowerment (WPE) program seeks to empower women and girls in conflict-affected areas to lead safer, more resilient lives by expanding their access to protection services, strengthening their participation in decision-making, building the capacity of local women's rights organizations, and ensuring that gender equality and the prevention of violence against women and girls (VAWG) are central to humanitarian planning and response. Under the program's Safety Outcome 4, which holds that the social norms of community members support the rights of diverse women and girls and prevent and condemn VAWG, the program works to reduce VAWG and promote positive behavior change through evidence-based approaches. In Ethiopia, this work sits within the POWER program (2025–2027), supported by Irish Aid. POWER pursues holistic GBV prevention and response across Burundi, Ethiopia, Kenya, Somalia, South Sudan and Sudan, delivered through strengthened women-led organizations. Its design reflects a set of deliberate commitments: at least 25 percent of funding flowing directly to partners, adherence to the PEERS principles for equitable partnership, women-led safety audits, a dedicated emergency response pillar, and a partnership learning pillar. This consultancy contributes directly to Sub-outcome 2 of the Irish Aid project. The EMAP+ (Engaging Men through Accountable Practice Plus) methodology focuses on transforming harmful masculinities and promoting accountability among men and boys in order to prevent VAWG. To ensure that the EMAP+ Resource Package is relevant and effective in the Ethiopian context, the program will engage a consultant to lead the adaptation, review and finalization of the EMAP+ materials. The assignment’s center of gravity is quality, learning, and carrying program evidence into humanitarian policy and practice, rather than day-to-day implementation in a single country. The adaptation of EMAP+ for Ethiopia is meant to produce a contextually sound curriculum for Ethiopia while generating transferable learning about how EMAP+ is adapted, learning that can inform other POWER countries and IRC's wider protection work. Consistent with POWER's partnership learning pillar, the contextualization is documented so that the reasoning, and not only the finished product, is available to others. In this consultancy that intent is kept deliberately light: it is met through clear documentation of the adaptation decisions rather than through a separate toolkit. Purpose of the consultancy To support the WPE program and the global VPRU in adapting, reviewing and finalizing the EMAP+ Resource Package for the Ethiopian context under the POWER program, and to capture the learning from that adaptation in a form that strengthens quality across POWER countries and supports the translation of program evidence into humanitarian policy and practice. The consultant will refine the overall resource package, validate its relevance through remote engagement with the IRC Ethiopia team and partners, and document the adaptation decisions taken so that the process is traceable and reusable. This consultancy contributes directly to the achievement of Sub-outcome 2 of the Irish Aid project. Specific objectives of the consultancy Adapt, review and finalize the EMAP+ Resource Package (the implementation guide, the training guide, and the resource package for women and men) to ensure contextual relevance for Ethiopia and alignment with the PO

title: Copyeditor
description: EDT are looking for four (4) Ethiopian consultants for copy-editing and proofreading in-service and pre-service teacher training material for a short term consultancy assignment. As part of the Leaders in Teaching Ethiopia (LiTE) programme we have developed a substantial number of in-service and pre-service teacher training modules to support teacher professional development and improve the quality of secondary education in Ethiopia. These modules have undergone technical review and now require professional copy editing and proofreading to ensure they are clear, consistent, linguistically accurate, and ready for implementation. The total volume of material requiring editorial review is estimated at approximately 1,900 pages. To ensure timely completion while maintaining high editorial standards, LiTE intends to engage four (4) qualified copy-editing consultants who will work concurrently on assigned batches of materials. The consultants will review and edit assigned modules to improve grammar, spelling, punctuation, clarity, consistency, readability, and adherence to agreed editorial standards while preserving the approved technical content and intended meaning. The assignment does not include substantive technical review, validation of technical content, or redesign of training materials. For planning purposes, the level of effort is estimated using an editing rate of approximately 500 pages to be edited in 5 days, although productivity may vary depending on the complexity and quality of the materials. The Copy-editing Consultants will be responsible for: Copy editing and proofreading assigned in-service and pre-service teacher training modules. Correcting grammar, spelling, punctuation, capitalization, sentence structure, word choice, and usage. Improving clarity, readability, flow, and consistency without changing the intended technical meaning. Standardizing terminology, abbreviations, acronyms, headings, subheadings, numbering, and editorial conventions. Ensuring consistency across modules, sections, activities, instructions, examples, tables, captions, and learning materials. Identifying and correcting typographical errors, duplicated or missing words, incomplete sentences, and inconsistent references. Reviewing learning activities, instructions, examples, and explanatory text for clarity and accuracy. Reviewing tables and structured content for editorial consistency. Checking internal references, numbering, labels, and cross-references. Flagging technical inconsistencies, ambiguities, contradictions, and content requiring technical review. Applying agreed editorial and formatting standards consistently across assigned materials. Proofreading revised files after feedback has been incorporated. You should have A bachelor's degree in English, Communications, Journalism, Publishing, Education, Linguistics, or a related field. Proven experience in copy editing, proofreading, publishing, editorial review, or a related discipline. Demonstrated experience editing educational, curriculum, training, technical, research, or development-sector materials. Excellent written English skills. Strong knowledge of English grammar, punctuation, spelling, syntax, style, and editorial conventions I nterested consultants should submit the following information. You will be asked to submit the information when you complete the application form. Please apply by 14th September An updated CV highlighting relevant experience. A brief technical proposal outlining your approach, methodology, quality assurance process, and work plan. An indication of availability and anticipated editing capacity (pages per week). At least two samples of previous editing work, preferably involving education, curriculum, training, technical, or development-sector materials. A proposed professional fee or daily rate. Contact details for at least two professional references.
